entries.full_description: Default binary path for all tasks. None means each ExecutorTask returned by arrange() must carry its own binary_path, otherwise the task fails with a clear error.

entries.full_description: Environment variables passed to all executor subprocesses. Merged on top of the (filtered) parent process environment. Per-task env vars from ExecutorTask.env override these on conflict.

entries.description: When True, the parent process env is passed to subprocesses (with deny patterns applied — see env_inherit_deny).
entries.full_description: When True, the parent process env is passed to subprocesses (with deny patterns applied — see env_inherit_deny). Set False to run subprocesses with ONLY ExecutorConfig.env + ExecutorTask.env — fully isolated from parent env.

entries.description: Case-insensitive fnmatch patterns against parent env var names.
entries.full_description: Case-insensitive fnmatch patterns against parent env var names. Matching vars are NOT inherited by subprocesses, even when env_inherit_parent is True. Deliberately narrower than the recorder redaction list: a pattern here WITHHOLDS the variable from your binary, so names with common non-secret uses (AUTH_SERVICE_URL, CERT_PATH, PRIVATE_SUBNET) are excluded. Set to [] to fully trust the parent environment.

entries.description: Maximum concurrent subprocesses.
entries.full_description: Maximum concurrent subprocesses. Tasks beyond this limit wait in a queue.

entries.description: Wall-clock time limit per subprocess, a whole number of seconds.
entries.full_description: Wall-clock time limit per subprocess, a whole number of seconds. A process exceeding it is killed and treated as a failure.

entries.description: Most stdout kept per task.
entries.full_description: Most stdout kept per task. 0 (the default) = no limit. When a process writes more, the kept prefix is cut at a UTF-8 character boundary, the rest is read and discarded (the process is never blocked on a full pipe), and ExecutorResult.stdout_truncated is set. Useful when subprocesses can emit very large output.

entries.description: Most stderr kept per task.
entries.full_description: Most stderr kept per task. 0 (the default) = no limit. Same semantics as max_stdout, applied to the stderr stream; sets ExecutorResult.stderr_truncated on cut.

entries.description: Maximum messages collected per arrange() window.
entries.full_description: Maximum messages collected per arrange() window. Larger windows allow more batching in arrange(); smaller windows reduce latency.

entries.description: Maximum retry attempts per failed task (0 = no retries).
entries.full_description: Maximum retry attempts per failed task (0 = no retries). A task runs at most max_retries + 1 times.

entries.description: What the default on_error returns when a task fails for good: 'skip' drops the task; 'dlq' writes its source message to the DLQ and ends the message.
entries.full_description: What the default on_error returns when a task fails for good: 'skip' drops the task; 'dlq' writes its source message to the DLQ and ends the message.

entries.description: Longest wait for in-flight executor tasks to finish during graceful shutdown or partition revocation, a whole number of seconds.
entries.full_description: Longest wait for in-flight executor tasks to finish during graceful shutdown or partition revocation, a whole number of seconds. Set lower to speed up shutdown; set at least as high as task_timeout if you rely on clean final commits for every in-flight task. When drain times out, the still-running tasks are cancelled — their subprocess process group is killed so the executor slot is freed at once — and their offsets are NOT committed (those messages will replay on restart — at-least-once).

entries.description: Pause threshold multiplier: Kafka consumption pauses when total queued messages reach max_executors * this value.
entries.full_description: Pause threshold multiplier: Kafka consumption pauses when total queued messages reach max_executors * this value.

entries.description: Resume threshold multiplier: Kafka consumption resumes when total queued messages drop to max(1, max_executors * this value).
entries.full_description: Resume threshold multiplier: Kafka consumption resumes when total queued messages drop to max(1, max_executors * this value).

entries.description: Worker threads in asyncio's default to_thread executor, from 1 to 512.
entries.full_description: Worker threads in asyncio's default to_thread executor, from 1 to 512. Null (the default) keeps Python's own sizing, min(32, cpu_count + 4). Set an explicit value when handler I/O concurrency is capped by the pool — e.g. many-core hosts doing wide blocking filesystem fan-out. Blocking I/O releases the GIL, so large values are legitimate here (unlike threads.offload); the trade-off is pressure on the storage behind the calls.

entries.description: Worker threads in the shared offload pool, from 1 to 32.
entries.full_description: Worker threads in the shared offload pool, from 1 to 32. Null (the default) sizes the pool from the executor pool: ceil(executor.max_executors / 4), with a minimum of 2 — e.g. pool 8 -> 2 threads, 9 -> 3, 13 -> 4. Calls beyond this many concurrent offloaded computations queue (FIFO) and show up in the drakkar_offload_queued gauge. More threads do not speed up pure-Python work (GIL); set an explicit value only when several partitions routinely offload at once and queueing delay matters, or when the offloaded code releases the GIL (numpy, compiled extensions).

entries.description: What happens when the retry budget of a delivery is spent: 'dlq' writes the source message to the DLQ and ends the message; 'skip' drops this sink's payloads and goes on.

entries.description: Budget for one sink delivery, including the framework-internal transient retries.
entries.full_description: Budget for one sink delivery, including the framework-internal transient retries. A sink whose server stops answering while the TCP connection stays open would otherwise block its partition forever: the circuit breaker only sees a failure when a call returns. Sinks whose driver supports it also use this value for their own socket or command timeout, so the driver reports a specific error first. Applies to close() during shutdown as well.

entries.description: Bound on the producer flush that ends every delivery.
entries.full_description: Bound on the producer flush that ends every delivery. Without one, librdkafka flushes with no deadline and a wedged broker blocks the call until message.timeout.ms (300s by default) — and it blocks a producer executor thread while doing it, so a few stuck deliveries starve every other delivery on the same producer. On expiry the delivery fails with a transient error, which is what lets the circuit breaker see the outage. Kept deliberately generous: this is a last resort, not a latency target.

entries.full_description: Raw librdkafka properties for the DLQ producer, merged after the connection's client_config; the DLQ wins on a shared key. Reserved keys are rejected at config load.

entries.description: Bound on the producer flush that ends every DLQ write.
entries.full_description: Bound on the producer flush that ends every DLQ write. Same rationale as flush_timeout of a Kafka sink, and it matters more here: the DLQ is the last resort, so a DLQ write that blocks for message.timeout.ms stalls the partition it was meant to rescue. On expiry the write is reported as unconfirmed and the affected offsets stall.

entries.description: Strategy when no DLQ record can be written.
entries.full_description: Strategy when no DLQ record can be written. 'drop' logs CRITICAL, counts the loss, commits the offset, and keeps the pipeline moving; 'stall' leaves the offset uncommitted and pauses the partition until restart — no loss, at the cost of consumer lag.

entries.description: Folder for this worker's own files (live recorder file, cache file, crash marker).
entries.full_description: Folder for this worker's own files (live recorder file, cache file, crash marker). Only this worker opens them. The worker creates it with mode 0700. Empty: no own files and no cache file; with recorder.enabled and provider sqlite the load fails.

entries.description: Folder that every worker of the cluster sees (for example a ReadWriteMany volume): registry cards, sealed history, archives and merge results.
entries.full_description: Folder that every worker of the cluster sees (for example a ReadWriteMany volume): registry cards, sealed history, archives and merge results. Empty means the same folder as dir, which is right for workers on one host.

entries.description: Durable recording in the store provider names.
entries.full_description: Durable recording in the store provider names. Off, nothing is written to a file or a table; with the UI on, the recorder still holds the recent events in memory for it.

entries.description: Where durable recording goes: sqlite writes recorder files into storage.dir, which must be set; postgres writes a table named by the postgres block, and storage.dir may be empty.
entries.full_description: Where durable recording goes: sqlite writes recorder files into storage.dir, which must be set; postgres writes a table named by the postgres block, and storage.dir may be empty.

entries.description: Time between recorder flushes, a whole number of seconds: the tick of the memory stage and of the file or Postgres stage.
entries.full_description: Time between recorder flushes, a whole number of seconds: the tick of the memory stage and of the file or Postgres stage.

entries.description: Rows the intake holds, and the file or Postgres queue too.
entries.full_description: Rows the intake holds, and the file or Postgres queue too. When full, the oldest are evicted and counted in drakkar_recorder_dropped_events_total.

entries.description: Keep recorder events in memory for this long.
entries.full_description: Keep recorder events in memory for this long.

entries.description: Row cap per executor slot: the store holds at most this many rows times executor.max_executors.
entries.full_description: Row cap per executor slot: the store holds at most this many rows times executor.max_executors. The cap does not scale with the window; a longer window needs a larger value (rows per executor per window is about 4 x window / average task seconds).

entries.description: Budget for the data in the memory store (pages in use), from 16MiB to 512MiB.
entries.full_description: Budget for the data in the memory store (pages in use), from 16MiB to 512MiB. It bounds the data, not the memory the store holds; free pages and one write stage can exceed it. At most 512MiB so the store stays under the 1 GiB limit of the SQLite in-memory database.

entries.description: Write processing events.
entries.full_description: Write processing events. Off, no event row goes anywhere, runtime health events included: the live WebSocket view still streams, but History, Trace, and task queries return nothing.

entries.full_description: Write the worker config snapshot to the worker_config table, so every recorder file names the worker and cluster that wrote it (history, merges, archives).

entries.description: Keep subprocess stdout/stderr content in task events.
entries.full_description: Keep subprocess stdout/stderr content in task events. Off drops output content from all of them.

entries.description: Keep each task's stdin content (capped at max_stdin) in the task_started event metadata, so the debug UI can show exactly what a task consumed.
entries.full_description: Keep each task's stdin content (capped at max_stdin) in the task_started event metadata, so the debug UI can show exactly what a task consumed. Off by default: on a high-fan-out workload stdin is the largest payload the recorder would write. Failed tasks always keep their stdin (capped) on the task_failed event, regardless of this flag.

entries.description: Size cap for kept stdin content (stdin, and the always-on failed-task capture).
entries.full_description: Size cap for kept stdin content (stdin, and the always-on failed-task capture). 0 = no limit. A cut is flagged as stdin_truncated in the event metadata.

entries.description: Shortest task duration whose task event is written at all.
entries.full_description: Shortest task duration whose task event is written at all. 0 writes everything.

entries.description: Shortest task duration whose args/stdout/stderr go into the written event.
entries.full_description: Shortest task duration whose args/stdout/stderr go into the written event. Faster tasks keep their row without output data.

entries.description: Environment variable names captured into the worker_config table — for recording deployment metadata like GIT_SHA or K8S_POD_NAME.
entries.full_description: Environment variable names captured into the worker_config table — for recording deployment metadata like GIT_SHA or K8S_POD_NAME.

entries.full_description: Accept handler annotations (self.annotate(...)) and write them to the events table.

entries.description: Size cap for one annotation payload; larger payloads are dropped whole.
entries.full_description: Size cap for one annotation payload; larger payloads are dropped whole. 0 = no limit.

entries.full_description: Total annotation size one hook invocation may write; further payloads are dropped. 0 = no limit.

entries.full_description: Consecutive failed flush attempts tolerated per batch before it is dropped (counted in drakkar_recorder_flush_batches_dropped_total).

entries.full_description: Periodically snapshot worker counters (uptime, partitions, pool utilization, queue depth) to the worker_state table.

entries.full_description: Time between worker_state snapshots and between resource samples, a whole number of seconds; also the heartbeat cadence worker liveness is judged by. Without provider sqlite, resource samples come every 10s.

entries.full_description: Fold sealed recorder files into one compressed archive per window, then delete the files. The archive covers the whole cluster with autodiscover on and storage.shared_dir set, else only this worker's files. Off, nothing removes sealed files.

entries.full_description: A window is archived this long after it ends, so late files of that window are still in it; a whole number of hours, >= recorder.sqlite.rotation_interval.

entries.full_description: How long archives are kept before deletion, a whole number of days. Defaults to 30 days so a worker cannot fill its disk unattended. 0 = keep archives for ever (a startup warning names the choice); any other value must cover due_after plus one window.

entries.full_description: The archive pass deletes merge results from the UI older than this. 0 = never.

entries.full_description: Time between archive slots, aligned to the epoch, a whole number of seconds and at least 30s. Give at most one of interval and cron; with neither, a slot every 1h. At each slot one worker of the cluster runs an archive pass, or each worker runs one over its own files.

entries.full_description: Five-field UTC cron expression for the archive slots, instead of interval. Give at most one of interval and cron.

entries.full_description: Lease of the archive slot, a whole number of seconds from 40 to 86400. The holder refreshes it while its pass runs; a lease that nobody refreshed for this long is taken over. Not used by a pass over a worker's own files.

entries.full_description: An archive work file older than this belongs to a dead archiver and is removed. At least 60s.

entries.full_description: How long the table keeps history, a whole number of hours from 1h to 168h. Read only when this worker creates the table; after that the value stored with the table rules. At most 168h: one partition per hour, and a trace search visits every partition.

entries.full_description: Send the stdout and stderr columns to Postgres. Off, both columns are written as NULL, except the stderr of a task_failed row, which is always kept.

entries.full_description: Largest total size of the table: 0 = no limit, or at least 64MiB. The partition upkeep drops the oldest hours until the table is under it, but never the current hour or later ones. entries.description: Run the runtime health monitor: heartbeat lag tracking, stall stack sampling, and the data behind the debug UI's Runtime tab.
entries.full_description: Run the runtime health monitor: heartbeat lag tracking, stall stack sampling, and the data behind the debug UI's Runtime tab.

entries.description: Heartbeat interval.
entries.full_description: Heartbeat interval. Lag is measured as how late each tick fires; the sampler thread also checks heartbeat age at this interval. Smaller values narrow the attribution blind spot for short blocks at slightly more (still negligible) wakeups.

entries.description: Lag above this marks the runtime 'degraded'.
entries.full_description: Lag above this marks the runtime 'degraded'. Recovery to 'healthy' needs several consecutive clean ticks (hysteresis), so a flapping loop does not spam state transitions.

entries.description: Heartbeat age above this marks the runtime 'stalled' and starts stack sampling: the sampler thread captures what the runtime thread is executing until the heartbeat resumes.
entries.full_description: Heartbeat age above this marks the runtime 'stalled' and starts stack sampling: the sampler thread captures what the runtime thread is executing until the heartbeat resumes. Each stall becomes one runtime_stall recorder event with the stacks.

entries.description: Maximum distinct stack traces captured per stall.
entries.full_description: Maximum distinct stack traces captured per stall. Repeated samples of the same location collapse into one entry with a count; further distinct stacks past the cap are dropped.

entries.description: Interval between runtime_health sample events written to the flight recorder for cross-restart history.
entries.full_description: Interval between runtime_health sample events written to the flight recorder for cross-restart history. The fine-grained lag sparkline comes from an in-memory ring buffer instead and costs no database writes.

entries.description: Length of the in-memory lag history ring buffer (one max/avg aggregate per second) served to the debug UI sparkline, a whole number of seconds and at least 1m.
entries.full_description: Length of the in-memory lag history ring buffer (one max/avg aggregate per second) served to the debug UI sparkline, a whole number of seconds and at least 1m.

entries.description: Maximum length of one lag episode, at least 10s.
entries.full_description: Maximum length of one lag episode, at least 10s. An episode spans the time the runtime is degraded or stalled; on recovery (or at this cap, for incidents that outlive it) the monitor writes one runtime_lag_episode event with aggregated stacks and a verdict — blocked, cpu_bound, starved, or inconclusive.

entries.description: Opt-in flight-recorder profiler: the sampler thread records a runtime_probe event with the runtime thread's stack every stack_probe_interval, regardless of health state.
entries.full_description: Opt-in flight-recorder profiler: the sampler thread records a runtime_probe event with the runtime thread's stack every stack_probe_interval, regardless of health state. Useful for tuning production workloads and post-incident analysis; off by default because it writes events for as long as the worker runs.

entries.description: Time between runtime_probe events while stack_probe_enabled is on.
entries.full_description: Time between runtime_probe events while stack_probe_enabled is on.

entries.description: Run the HTTP server: /healthz, /readyz and the peer route.
entries.full_description: Run the HTTP server: /healthz, /readyz and the peer route. Off means no listener at all, so nothing answers the Kubernetes probes, and ui.enabled and autodiscover.enabled must both be false.

entries.description: Bind address for the HTTP server.
entries.full_description: Bind address for the HTTP server. Use 0.0.0.0 to expose on all interfaces.

entries.description: Port for the HTTP server.
entries.full_description: Port for the HTTP server.

entries.description: Externally reachable URL of this worker's HTTP server.
entries.full_description: Externally reachable URL of this worker's HTTP server. Peers and browsers reach the worker through it, and the registry card carries it. Empty derives http://<outbound ip>:<port>/.

entries.description: Serve the UI: the pages, the bundle fetch, the debug and data routes, /ws and the docs.
entries.full_description: Serve the UI: the pages, the bundle fetch, the debug and data routes, /ws and the docs. It needs api.enabled. Off: those routes answer 404, no bundle is fetched, and the recorder keeps no memory store.

entries.description: Bearer token for the UI routes. **Empty (the default) disables auth** entirely — every UI endpoint (including database download, merge, and message-probe) is reachable without credentials and the WebSocket live-event stream skips the token check (the Origin check always runs).
entries.full_description: Bearer token for the UI routes. **Empty (the default) disables auth** entirely — every UI endpoint (including database download, merge, and message-probe) is reachable without credentials and the WebSocket live-event stream skips the token check (the Origin check always runs). This is a deliberate opt-in design: no endpoint stops a worker, replays Kafka messages, mutates sinks, or commits offsets, and Drakkar is intended for deployment inside a private contour (VPC / internal cluster / operator-only ingress). Most endpoints are read-only, but the probe and merge routes are not — close those with ``probe.enabled`` / ``merge_enabled``, which act independently of this token. A startup warning fires whenever the UI is enabled without a token so the unauthenticated posture is visible in logs, naming whichever side-effecting endpoint is still enabled. When set to a non-empty value, protected HTTP endpoints require an ``Authorization: Bearer <token>`` header or ``?token=<token>`` query parameter; WebSocket connections without a valid token are closed with code 4401, and the Origin header is validated against ``allowed_origins`` (or the request Host header if that list is empty). /healthz, /readyz and the peer route stay public. Comparison uses ``secrets.compare_digest`` to avoid timing side-channels. Trailing/leading whitespace is stripped on load to avoid silent mismatches when YAML accidentally quotes spaces.

entries.description: Explicit allowlist of browser origins for /ws and the fan-out reads.
entries.full_description: Explicit allowlist of browser origins for /ws and the fan-out reads. A non-empty list is strict: nothing outside it connects, token or not. Empty list with a token set means same-origin only. Empty list with no token allows the cross-origin handshakes the cluster view needs but rejects a page that is not itself on loopback asking for a worker that is — a peer worker is never at the browser own loopback address, only a web page reaching into the machine is. A missing Origin header (curl, websocat) is always accepted; a browser cannot omit it.

entries.description: Maximum rows returned to the web UI in list views.
entries.full_description: Maximum rows returned to the web UI in list views.

entries.description: Shortest task duration broadcast to the live UI over WebSocket.
entries.full_description: Shortest task duration broadcast to the live UI over WebSocket. Failed tasks always appear. 0 shows all tasks.

entries.description: Path to a deployment-provided JS module of custom cell renderers, served as-is at ``GET /api/v1/ui/renderers.js``.
entries.full_description: Path to a deployment-provided JS module of custom cell renderers, served as-is at ``GET /api/v1/ui/renderers.js``. Empty (the default) disables the feature — the route then 404s and identity reports ``custom_renderers: false``. When set, the file must exist at startup or the worker fails to boot; its content is trusted the same as any other backend config (it runs same-origin in the operator UI).

entries.description: Serve ``POST /api/v1/debug/probe``.
entries.full_description: Serve ``POST /api/v1/debug/probe``. This is the one UI endpoint that runs caller-supplied bytes through the live handler and the real executor subprocess pool, so it is neither read-only nor free: it competes with production traffic for executor slots. Set to false to serve 403 instead, whatever ``auth_token`` says: a deployment that cannot set a token can still close the endpoint, and a deployment that has one can still close it as defence in depth. Probes never write sinks, recorder rows, cache entries, or offsets, so switching it off costs no pipeline behaviour.

entries.description: Maximum probe.set/append/update calls recorded per probe run.
entries.full_description: Maximum probe.set/append/update calls recorded per probe run. The first write past the cap records one ProbeError; further writes are dropped silently.

entries.description: Maximum total serialized size of all probe-details writes per probe run.
entries.full_description: Maximum total serialized size of all probe-details writes per probe run. Past it, writes are dropped like the max_writes cap.

entries.description: Serve ``POST /api/v1/debug/merge``.
entries.full_description: Serve ``POST /api/v1/debug/merge``. This is the one UI endpoint that writes to disk: each call creates a new ``merged-<ts>-<token>.db`` in the ``merged`` folder of the shared folder, kept for ``recorder.archive.merged_retention``. Set to false to serve 403 instead — independently of ``auth_token``, per the reasoning on ``probe.enabled``.

entries.description: Serve ``GET /api/v1/debug/kafka/*`` — ad-hoc reads of the configured topics (source, dlq, and each Kafka sink by instance name; never an arbitrary topic).
entries.full_description: Serve ``GET /api/v1/debug/kafka/*`` — ad-hoc reads of the configured topics (source, dlq, and each Kafka sink by instance name; never an arbitrary topic). Reads use assign()-only consumers that join no consumer group and commit no offsets, so they are invisible to the pipeline. Set to false to serve 403 instead — independently of ``auth_token``, per the reasoning on ``probe.enabled``. When the resolved Kafka security of any readable topic is not PLAINTEXT while ``auth_token`` is empty, startup logs a warning naming the exposed aliases (the API stays available — gate it with ``auth_token`` or close it here).

entries.description: Serve the consume-pause API (``/api/v1/debug/consume-pause``) and show the pause control on the Live page.
entries.full_description: Serve the consume-pause API (``/api/v1/debug/consume-pause``) and show the pause control on the Live page. Off by default: pausing stops message intake for the chosen duration, which is a production-affecting act — enable it deliberately, for debug-friendly deployments.

entries.full_description: Preset pause durations offered as one-click buttons on the Live page, each a whole number of seconds from 1s to 1h. The API itself accepts any duration in that range regardless of the presets.

entries.description: Base URL of the Prometheus server used for UI links.
entries.full_description: Base URL of the Prometheus server used for UI links. Empty shows no Prometheus links.

entries.description: Rate interval used in PromQL rate() expressions in UI links (e.g. '1m', '5m', '15m').
entries.full_description: Rate interval used in PromQL rate() expressions in UI links (e.g. '1m', '5m', '15m').

entries.description: PromQL label filter for worker-scoped queries, with {worker_id}, {cluster_name}, {metrics_port}, and {debug_port} template variables.
entries.full_description: PromQL label filter for worker-scoped queries, with {worker_id}, {cluster_name}, {metrics_port}, and {debug_port} template variables. Empty defaults to instance="{hostname}:{metrics_port}".

entries.description: PromQL label filter for cluster-wide queries, same template variables as worker_label.
entries.full_description: PromQL label filter for cluster-wide queries, same template variables as worker_label. Empty hides cluster-wide links.

entries.description: Custom links shown in the dashboard navigation.
entries.full_description: Custom links shown in the dashboard navigation. Each entry is a dict with name and url keys; url supports the {worker_id}, {cluster_name}, {metrics_port}, and {debug_port} template variables.

entries.description: Named URL bases for probe-details link templates, e.g. ``{jira: 'https://jira.internal.example.com'}``.
entries.full_description: Named URL bases for probe-details link templates, e.g. ``{jira: 'https://jira.internal.example.com'}``. A template such as ``{jira}/browse/{value}`` resolves ``{jira}`` from this map, so code declares the link shape once and each environment supplies its own hosts. A base referenced by a registered layout but missing here logs one startup warning and the UI renders plain text for it.

entries.description: Resolve and serve the drakkar-ui bundle.
entries.full_description: Resolve and serve the drakkar-ui bundle. Off means no UI at all (no fetch, no cache read): the JSON API, the health probes and the event WebSocket keep working, and page requests answer 503.

entries.description: The "owner/name" GitHub repo that publishes UI bundles.
entries.full_description: The "owner/name" GitHub repo that publishes UI bundles. Empty disables fetching — only an already-cached bundle is served, which is how an air-gapped deployment pins itself to a bundle staged with the drakkar-ui CLI.

entries.description: Known-good UI release tag this backend is built against (e.g. "v1.2.0"); the contract is API-major compatible.
entries.full_description: Known-good UI release tag this backend is built against (e.g. "v1.2.0"); the contract is API-major compatible. Empty means "no pinned version".

entries.description: Bundle cache root override.
entries.full_description: Bundle cache root override. Empty uses the per-user cache dir ($XDG_CACHE_HOME/drakkar/ui, falling back to ~/.cache/drakkar/ui — the conventional per-user cache location, so co-located workers share one cache).

entries.description: Resolve the latest release tag on startup instead of only the pinned version (the "check for a new version" toggle).
entries.full_description: Resolve the latest release tag on startup instead of only the pinned version (the "check for a new version" toggle). Already-cached versions are never re-downloaded — release tags are immutable.

entries.description: Directory of a prebuilt static docs site served at /docs/.
entries.full_description: Directory of a prebuilt static docs site served at /docs/. Empty disables the feature.

entries.description: Nav-entry label and default drawer heading in the UI.
entries.full_description: Nav-entry label and default drawer heading in the UI.

entries.full_description: Contextual anchors opening the named docs page from matching UI surfaces.
